# Asking What Matters: Disagreement-Guided Ambiguity Detection for Interactive Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#disguad)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-19**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.21645v1) · arXiv:2611.21645v1; primary record and PDF dated 14 October 2026, listed under 18 November 2026 in the inspected cs.DB announcement page

**Reading coverage:** All 19 PDF pages: Sections 1–5, AI-use statement, references, Appendices A–D, all four figures and four tables, scoring/state equations, case study and complete reported prompts. Visually inspected Figures 1–4 and associated coverage/ablation tables on PDF pages 2, 4, 8 and 9. Separately checked primary submission and announcement records.

## Research question

A fluent clarification question may address an apparent uncertainty without changing the SQL decisions that matter to the intended answer.

## Method

Extracts query-term anchors and generates eight contrastive SQL interpretations across subgoal, relational-route, definition and single-axis probes. Canonical component differences are aggregated and mapped to askable concepts. A priority heuristic and record of previously asked targets select deterministic clarification templates; probes are not final-answer candidates.

## Evaluation

Uses BIRD-Interact Lite and Full in conversational mode with two backbones, each also serving as user simulator and ambiguity module. Reports executable-test success and normalized task reward, lexical gold-target coverage, probe-budget sensitivity and ablations. DAIL-SQL and DIN-SQL receive the resulting dialogues with their generators fixed.

## What the results support

Normalized reward improves by 4.40–8.97 points over the original interaction policy, with further gains when the dialogues feed static frameworks. Query-term extraction and disagreement mapping contribute larger ablation differences than any single probe family.

## Limits and qualifications

Unevaluated probe validity and structural differences can confound genuine ambiguity with generation error or equivalent SQL. Coverage is string/token matching, not confirmed resolution, and its table/figure aggregate values differ. Shared-model simulation lacks real-user validation. Extra model-call costs, run variability and some priority configuration details are not quantified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Offers a concrete mechanism for selecting clarification targets while exposing a boundary between structural disagreement, lexical coverage and semantic success.
